name: Pharma and AI Biotech Partnerships
blurb: How drugmakers buy AI discovery: collaborations, milestones and royalties.
title: Pharma and AI Biotech Partnerships
answer: Most large drugmakers access AI discovery through partnerships with AI biotechs rather than building everything in house. Typical deals pay a modest upfront sum and much larger milestone payments tied to candidates reaching the clinic and market, so most headline values depend on future success.

reading.body:
Most large drugmakers buy AI drug discovery through partnerships rather than building it in house, and most headline deal values are contingent on future milestones.

The deal structure carries the real information. A modest upfront payment plus large milestone payments tied to candidates reaching the clinic and market means the announced total is a ceiling, not a commitment. The upfront sum and the number of programmes are the better signals of how much the partner believes in the platform.

Two developments in the data show the two shapes this takes. Iambic and Takeda is a platform applied to named target areas in oncology, gastrointestinal and inflammation. Lilly and NVIDIA is a co-innovation lab pairing biology with compute, which points at the infrastructure layer underneath discovery rather than a single pipeline.

The data does not give deal values, so it cannot show whether upfronts are rising or falling, nor how many partnerships fail to produce a candidate. It covers the structure of these deals and two recent examples, not their economics.

sections.body: Read deal values as mostly contingent. The upfront payment and the number of programmes are better signals of how much a partner believes in the platform.
